Simulate responses from a fitted model

Source: R/gamm4-methods.R, R/gjrm-diagnostics.R, R/simulate-methods.R
simulate.Rd

Generate replicated responses using fitted parameter values. posterior_samples() also includes uncertainty in the coefficients. See diagnostic_support.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'gamm4'
simulate(object, nsim = 1, seed = NULL, conditioning = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gamlss'
simulate(object, nsim = 1L, seed = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gam'
simulate(
  object,
  nsim = 1,
  seed = NULL,
  data = newdata,
  weights = NULL,
  ...,
  newdata = NULL,
  family_index = NULL,
  envir = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'gamm'
simulate(
  object,
  nsim = 1,
  seed = NULL,
  data = newdata,
  weights = NULL,
  ...,
  newdata = NULL,
  conditioning = NULL,
  envir = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'scam'
simulate(
  object,
  nsim = 1,
  seed = NULL,
  data = newdata,
  weights = NULL,
  ...,
  newdata = NULL,
  envir = NULL
)

Arguments

object

a fitted GAM, typically the result of a call to mgcv::gam(), mgcv::gamm(), or gamm4::gamm4().

nsim

numeric; number of response simulations to return.

seed

numeric; a random seed for the simulations.

conditioning

character or NULL; optional mixed-model conditioning mode. gamm4 defaults to "conditional", holding all fitted effects fixed. "gam_component" explicitly uses its extracted GAM. The existing gamm simulator retains its GAM-component default. Full mixed-model modes currently use fitting observations.

...

arguments passed to methods. simulate.gam() and simulate.scam() pass ... on to predict.gam(). As such you can pass additional arguments such as terms, exclude, to select which model terms are included in the predictions. This may be useful, for example, for excluding the effects of random effect terms.

data

data frame; new observations at which the posterior draws from the model should be evaluated. If not supplied, the data used to fit the model will be used for newdata, if available in object.

weights

numeric; response sampling weights. An explicit vector overrides the fitting weights; a single value applies to every observation. With data = NULL, the default is the fitted prior weights, except factor-valued binomial responses retain one Bernoulli trial per observation. Native gaulss() ignores fitting weights in its likelihood, so its default response weights are ones; explicit sampling weights still override this. With prediction data, the default is a vector of ones. For ordinary Gaussian and Gamma responses, larger weights reduce response variance (precision weights). For binomial responses, weights give integer trial counts. Include positions restored by na.exclude when supplying weights for fitting rows.

newdata

Deprecated. Use data instead.

family_index

numeric; for grouped-family models, one integer family index per requested prediction row. See Details.

envir

environment or NULL; functions and constants needed to evaluate model expressions in prediction data. With NULL, use the model's formula environment. Supply raw covariates in data.

Value

(Currently) A data frame with nsim columns.

Details

For simulate.gam() to function, the family component of the fitted model must contain, or be updatable to contain, the required random number generator. See mgcv::fix.family.rd().

With data = NULL, na.exclude restores excluded observations as NA in every simulation; na.omit returns retained observations only. Positions refer to the fitting data after any subset. Explicit data are evaluated independently of training exclusions: missing responses do not prevent simulation, while missing required predictors or weights yield NA. Prediction na.action in ... is honoured. Missing rows are never passed to the response random-number generator.

Inverse Gaussian models use a native generator with observation dispersion equal to the model dispersion divided by the prior weight, consistently with their CDF and quantile helpers. Weights must be non-negative; a zero weight with positive dispersion uses the limiting point mass at zero. An existing random generator supplied in the family's rd component is preserved.

For models fitted with mgcv::gfam(), each observation is simulated from its component family using that component's fitted scale and distribution parameters. With data = NULL, fitted family membership is used. For explicit data, supply family_index or the index in the model's response expression: the second column of a matrix response, the second argument of cbind(y, index), or a numeric index vector in place of a named matrix response. Actual response observations are not needed. Missing indices follow prediction na.action; invalid indices are errors. Explicit indices must agree with recoverable ones.

Grouped simulations return one numeric response per observation: binomial proportions (with integer trial counts supplied in weights), count responses, or ordered-category codes, as appropriate. Component random generators retain their usual treatment of prior weights. Ordered-categorical and ziP components are simulated from their latent predictors. General families with multiple linear predictors and matrix responses encoding censoring or binomial counts are outside the scope supported by gfam(). Scalar censored-family components produce draws from their uncensored latent distributions.

See also

gamm4_support

Author

Gavin L. Simpson

Examples

load_mgcv()
dat <- data_sim("eg1", n = 400, dist = "normal", scale = 2, seed = 2)
m1 <- gam(y ~ s(x0) + s(x1) + s(x2) + s(x3), data = dat, method = "REML")

sims <- simulate(m1, nsim = 5, seed = 42)
head(sims)
#>       sim_1     sim_2     sim_3     sim_4     sim_5
#> 1 11.445470 11.374304 10.098681  7.264881  8.796630
#> 2  6.510912  5.909584  9.057362  7.698084 11.444781
#> 3  3.837995  3.230610  3.550240  3.759380  4.774581
#> 4 12.361830 11.209226 10.714215 11.861957 10.746417
#> 5 14.851461 12.911440 11.356984 15.783913 15.106270
#> 6  5.921276  4.158963  5.520856  7.973614  9.654888
